search_log: Searched official-author and publisher combinations for “The Invisible Life of Addie LaRue” with “excerpt,” “first chapter,” and “read an extract”; opened Tor/Reactor’s authorized first-chapter text.
Searched the verified title with “point of view,” “third person,” “narrator,” and “third-person present”; opened the BookRags, Ohio Wesleyan ENG 250, and LitCharts analyses.

Searched for “epistolary,” “frame narrative,” “multiple narrators,” and “alternating point of view”; found focalization shifts between Addie and Henry, but no sustained change away from third-person base narration.
Opened the Macmillan title page; it verified the work and publisher but supplied synopsis rather than diagnostic person evidence, so it was not included as supporting evidence.
Ran targeted searches for the apparent first-person photography passage and spoken-address material; results did not establish either as an autonomous first- or second-person base section.
person_note: The controlling narrator is nonparticipating third person, chiefly close-limited through Addie and, in other chapters, Henry. Numerous event quotations render those characters’ private thoughts while naming them as she/he, and the authorized first chapter shows the same sustained structure. Whole-book structural sources explicitly confirm that focalization alternates between Addie and Henry while narrative person remains third. Apparent first person in q05225 and q05247 is local character language, as are the many dialogue quotations; generic “you” in aphorisms is not story-specific second-person narration. No credible evidence of a sustained first- or second-person base section remained.
